gloss: strength, ability, wealth, army; writhe, be in labour, tremble; whirl, dance; sand
summary: One spelling covering two older roots. חַיִל is strength: the might God girds a man with, the worth of a capable man or woman, the wealth strength gains, and the army that is a nation’s strength (Zec 4:6; Rut 3:11; Deu 8:17–18; Exo 14:28); Arabic ḥawl, ḥayl “strength, power” shows ḥ behind its ח. The verb חוּל is to writhe as a woman in labour, to bring forth, and to tremble before Yahweh (Isa 66:7–8; Psa 114:7), with חִיל “labour pain”; Akkadian ḫiālu “be in labour” and Ugaritic ḫl show ḫ, another older sound. The same verb whirls like a storm and dances (Jer 23:19; Jdg 21:21), whence מָחוֹל, מְחוֹלָה “dance”; חוֹל “sand” is kept with the root, its tie not yet understood.

words.gloss: strength, might; ability, worth; wealth; army, force
words.summary: Strength, and what strength is in a man, in his goods and in a nation: the might God gives, the ability or worth of a capable person, wealth, and an armed force. The construct is חֵיל.

senses.definition: Bodily, military or vital strength: the power to act, stand and prevail, which God gives and girds a man with, set beside כֹּחַ “power”.

evidence.note: “Not by חַיִל and not by כֹּחַ, but by my spirit, says Yahweh of hosts.”
“The bows of the mighty are broken, and the stumbling are girded with חָיִל.”
“The God who girds me with חָיִל.”
A king is not saved by רָב־חָיִל, a mighty man not delivered by רָב־כֹּחַ.
The horse does not deliver by its great חַיִל.
“Yahweh the Lord is my חַיִל; he makes my feet like hinds’ feet.”
They go from חַיִל to חָיִל.
If the iron is blunt, one must put forth more חֲיָלִים.
“Do not give your חַיִל to women.”
The fig tree and the vine give their חַיִל, their yield.
“The right hand of Yahweh does חָיִל.”

senses.definition: Strength of character and capability in a person: the able men fit to be set over others, the woman of worth, the man of valour. Used chiefly in the phrases אַנְשֵׁי חַיִל, אֵשֶׁת חַיִל, גִּבּוֹר חַיִל and בֶּן־חַיִל.

evidence.note: Choose אַנְשֵׁי־חַיִל who fear God, men of truth, hating unjust gain, to rule the people.
If you know אַנְשֵׁי־חַיִל among them, make them rulers over my cattle.
“All the gate of my people knows that you are אֵשֶׁת חָיִל.”
אֵשֶׁת־חַיִל is her husband’s crown, set against the one who causes shame.
“An אֵשֶׁת־חַיִל who can find? Her price is far above rubies.”
Boaz, אִישׁ גִּבּוֹר חַיִל.
If Adonijah proves a בֶּן־חַיִל, not a hair of his will fall.
“Yahweh is with you, גִּבּוֹר הֶחָיִל.”
Gatekeepers, אִישׁ־חַיִל בַּכֹּחַ לַעֲבֹדָה, able men with strength for the service.

senses.definition: What strength gains and holds: possessions, riches and the goods of a people or city, which can be plundered, trusted in or brought as tribute.

evidence.note: “My power and the might of my hand have made me this חַיִל.”
“It is he who gives you power to make חָיִל.”
Those who trust in their חַיִל and boast in the abundance of their riches, עָשְׁרָם.
The wise and the fool die alike and leave their חֵיל to others.
“If חַיִל increases, do not set your heart on it.”
If I rejoiced because my חֵיל was great.
All their חֵיל, their little ones and wives they took captive.
The sinner’s חֵיל is laid up for the righteous.
By your wisdom you have made yourself חַיִל, gold and silver in your treasuries.
The חֵיל of the nations will come to you.
“You will eat the חֵיל of the nations.”

senses.definition: A body of armed men, a nation’s strength in the field: Pharaoh’s chariots and horsemen, Israel’s and the Chaldeans’ armies; in the plural, the bands of fighting men.

evidence.note: The waters covered the chariots and horsemen of all Pharaoh’s חֵיל that came into the sea.
His horsemen and his חֵילוֹ overtook them by the sea.
“Pharaoh’s chariots and his חֵילוֹ he has cast into the sea.”
Joab, שַׂר־הַחַיִל, the commander of the army, sent to number the people.
The חֵיל of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and all his חֵיל was scattered from him.
Nebuchadnezzar and all his חֵילוֹ fought against Jerusalem.
שָׂרֵי הַחֲיָלִים, the captains of the forces in the field.
The slain lived and stood on their feet, חַיִל גָּדוֹל מְאֹד־מְאֹד.
Gog from the far north: a great company, חַיִל רָב.
Yahweh gives his voice before his חֵילוֹ.
“Your people are freewill offerings in the day of your חֵילֶךָ.”
The king sent with Nehemiah שָׂרֵי חַיִל and horsemen.

evidence.locator: חַיִל → δύναμις ×148 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Zec.4.6 חַיִל → δυνάμει; Psa.18.33, Psa.33.16 → δύναμιν; Rut.3.11 אֵשֶׁת חַיִל → γυνὴ δυνάμεως

evidence.note: “Holy spirit will come upon you, and δύναμις of the Most High will overshadow you” (Peshitta ܚܝܠܐ).
“You will receive δύναμις when the holy spirit has come upon you.”
The gospel is δύναμις of God for salvation.

evidence.locator: חַיִל → ἰσχύς ×20 (lemma count), e.g. Deu.33.11
חַיִל → πλοῦτος ×9 (lemma count), e.g. Job.20.15; Pro.31.3 חֵיל → πλοῦτον

evidence.note: “Your πλοῦτος has rotted.”

parallels.note: “Power”, beside חַיִל of a man’s strength and set with it against Yahweh’s spirit.
“Riches”, beside it in the sense of wealth.
“Abundance”: the abundance of the sea beside the wealth of the nations.

opposites.note: Yahweh’s spirit, set against human might as the means of his work.

evidence.note: “Israel עֹשֶׂה חָיִל.”
“Through God we will נַעֲשֶׂה־חָיִל.”
Power לַעֲשׂוֹת חָיִל, to get wealth.
“Do worthily in Ephrathah.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, the same word as the Hebrew: strength, and an army, including the host of heaven over which God does as he wills.

senses.definition: Strength and force; with בְּ, of a herald’s or king’s crying “with strength”, aloud.

evidence.note: They made the Jews cease בְּאֶדְרָע וְחָיִל, by arm and force.
The herald cried בְחָיִל, aloud.
The watcher cried בְחַיִל.
The king cried בְּחַיִל to bring in the enchanters.

senses.definition: An armed force, and the host of heaven over which God rules as over the inhabitants of the earth.

evidence.note: Mighty men גִּבָּרֵי־חַיִל who were בְחַיְלֵהּ, in his army.
He does according to his will בְּחֵיל שְׁמַיָּא and among the inhabitants of the earth.

words.summary: The rampart or outer wall of a city, beside חוֹמָה “wall”. Its link to the root is not certain: it may be a city’s strength, like חַיִל, or what goes around it (Arabic ḥawl “around”, recorded as possible).

senses.definition: The outer fortification of a city, against which a siege mound is raised, set beside its wall and citadels.

evidence.note: They cast up a mound against the city, and it stood בַּחֵל, against the rampart, while they battered the wall.
He made חֵל and חוֹמָה lament; they languish together.
“Salvation he appoints for walls and חֵל.”
“Set your heart לְחֵילָה, consider her citadels.”
“Peace be within your חֵיל, prosperity within your citadels.”
No-amon, whose חֵיל was the sea, the sea her wall.
The dogs will eat Jezebel בְּחֵל יִזְרְעֶאל.

words.gloss: writhe, be in labour, bring forth; tremble; whirl; dance; wait; be firm
words.summary: Chiefly to writhe as a woman in labour, to bring forth, and to tremble in fear before Yahweh; Akkadian ḫiālu and Ugaritic ḫl show ḫ behind this ח. It is also used of a storm or sword whirling and of dancing, of waiting, and in two verses of ways and prosperity that stand firm, which goes with חַיִל “strength” (ḥ). How the waiting is tied to the rest is not clear.

stems.gloss: writhe, be in labour; tremble; whirl; dance; wait; be firm

senses.definition: To twist in pain as a woman giving birth, and so of any anguish that seizes the body or heart.

evidence.note: “As a pregnant woman who draws near to give birth תָּחִיל, cries out in her pangs.”
“Before she writhed (תָּחִיל) she gave birth; before her pain came she delivered a male.”
“As soon as Zion חָלָה, she gave birth to her sons.”
“Sing, barren one who did not bear … who did not חָלָה.” Quoted in Gal 4:27 with ὠδίνουσα.
Isa 54:1 quoted: “Break forth and shout, you who are not in labour (ἡ οὐκ ὠδίνουσα).”
“Woe to him who says to a woman, What are you writhing with?” beside a father begetting.
“We were pregnant, we writhed, we gave birth as it were to wind.”
“Writhe and labour, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth.”
Pangs seize them; they writhe like a woman giving birth.
“My heart יָחִיל within me, and the terrors of death have fallen on me.”
Saul writhed greatly because of the archers.

senses.definition: To shake with fear before Yahweh’s presence: of people, the earth, mountains and waters.

evidence.note: “חוּלִי, earth, before the Lord, before the God of Jacob.”
“Do you not fear me? … Do you not tremble before me?” Parallel with יָרֵא.
The waters saw you and יָחִילוּ; the depths also quaked (יִרְגְּזוּ).
The peoples will hear the report of you, וְרָגְזוּ וְחָלוּ.
“Bow down to Yahweh in the splendour of holiness; חִילוּ before him, all the earth.”
“You struck them, but they did not חָלוּ.”

senses.definition: Of a storm, a sword or a curse: to whirl round and come down on someone.

evidence.note: A whirling (מִתְחוֹלֵל) storm: on the head of the wicked it יָחוּל.
The sword will whirl against his cities.
“Let it fall (יָחֻלוּ) on the head of Joab.”
Sodom was overthrown in a moment, and no hands חָלוּ on her.

senses.definition: To dance in the round dances (מְחֹלוֹת).

evidence.note: If the daughters of Shiloh come out לָחוּל בַּמְּחֹלוֹת, to dance in the dances.

senses.definition: To wait, stay. Its tie to the root’s other senses is not clear.

evidence.note: Eglon’s servants וַיָּחִילוּ עַד־בּוֹשׁ, waited until they were ashamed.

senses.definition: Of ways and prosperity: to stand firm and last.

evidence.note: The wicked man’s ways יָחִילוּ at all times; Yahweh’s judgments are far above him.
“Therefore his prosperity לֹא־יָחִיל, will not endure.”

senses.definition: To bring to birth: of a mother, of God bringing forth Israel and the earth, of Yahweh’s voice making the hinds calve, of the north wind bringing rain.

evidence.note: “Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah תְּחוֹלֶלְכֶם, who bore you.”
“The Rock that begot you (יְלָדְךָ) you forgot, the God מְחֹלְלֶךָ, who brought you forth.”
“Before the mountains were born, or you brought forth (וַתְּחוֹלֵל) the earth and the world.”
The voice of Yahweh makes the hinds calve.
“Do you watch when the hinds calve?”
The north wind brings forth rain.

senses.definition: To dance, in the participle, the dancing women.

evidence.note: They took wives מִן־הַמְּחֹלְלוֹת, from the dancers.

senses.definition: To wait for someone.

evidence.note: “The cause is before him, וּתְחוֹלֵל לוֹ, and you must wait for him.”

stems.gloss: be brought forth, be born; tremble

senses.definition: To be brought to birth: of a man born in iniquity, of wisdom brought forth before the hills.

evidence.note: “In iniquity I was brought forth (חוֹלָלְתִּי), and in sin my mother conceived me.”
Wisdom: “When there were no depths I was brought forth.”
“Before the hills I was brought forth.”
“Were you the first man born? Were you brought forth before the hills?”

senses.definition: To be made to tremble.

evidence.note: The Rephaim יְחוֹלָלוּ beneath the waters.

senses.definition: Of a storm, whirling.

evidence.note: סַעַר מִתְחוֹלֵל, a whirling storm.

senses.definition: To be in anguish.

evidence.note: All the days of the wicked he מִתְחוֹלֵל, is in pain.

senses.definition: To wait for Yahweh, beside being still before him.

evidence.note: “Be still before Yahweh, וְהִתְחוֹלֵל לוֹ, and wait for him; do not fret.”

senses.definition: To make something writhe or shake.

evidence.note: “The voice of Yahweh יָחִיל the wilderness; Yahweh יָחִיל the wilderness of Kadesh.”

senses.definition: To be brought to birth.

evidence.note: “Shall a land הֲיוּחַל, be brought forth, in one day?” beside a nation born at once.

senses.definition: To be in great distress.

evidence.note: When told of Mordecai, the queen וַתִּתְחַלְחַל מְאֹד.

senses.definition: To wait. The form may belong to יחל “wait”, which the same passage uses.

evidence.note: Noah וַיָּחֶל yet another seven days and again sent out the dove; Gen 8:12 has וַיִּיָּחֶל.

senses.definition: A participle whose sense the verse does not fix: an archer who wounds all, or a master who brings forth all.

evidence.note: רַב מְחוֹלֵל־כֹּל, beside hiring a fool and hiring passers-by.

evidence.locator: Isa.54.1 חָלָה → ὠδίνουσα; Isa.66.8 יוּחַל, חָלָה → ὤδινεν

evidence.note: Isa 54:1 quoted: ἡ οὐκ ὠδίνουσα.
“My little children, for whom I am again in labour (ὠδίνω) until Christ is formed in you.”
The woman cried out ὠδίνουσα, in pain to give birth.

evidence.locator: Psa.96.9 חִילוּ → σαλευθήτω; σαλεύω renders the verb ×2

evidence.note: “Whose voice then shook (ἐσάλευσεν) the earth.”

parallels.note: “Give birth”, beside it of a woman and of Zion.
“Quake”, beside it of peoples and the deep.
“Be still”, beside its sense of waiting for Yahweh.

words.summary: The pain of a woman in labour, and the anguish that seizes peoples and kings at a report, likened to it. Akkadian ḫīlū “labour pains” is the same word.

senses.definition: Pain like a woman’s in giving birth, seizing those who hear of coming disaster.

evidence.note: “Distress has seized us, חִיל כַּיּוֹלֵדָה, pain as of a woman giving birth.”
Trembling seized the kings there, חִיל כַּיּוֹלֵדָה.
The peoples heard and trembled; חִיל seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
The king of Babylon heard the report; distress seized him, חִיל like a woman giving birth.
“Why has חִיל seized you like a woman giving birth?”

evidence.locator: Exo.15.14, Psa.48.7, Jer.6.24 חִיל → ὠδῖνες

evidence.note: Sudden destruction comes on them as ἡ ὠδίν on a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
“All these are the beginning of ὠδίνων.”

phrases.gloss: pain like a woman giving birth

words.summary: A feminine form of חִיל, once. Its tokens are counted under חִיל, since the two words share one list of occurrences.

senses.definition: Pain that does not spare.

evidence.note: “I would exult בְחִילָה, in pain that does not spare, for I have not denied the words of the Holy One.”

words.summary: A doubled form of the root, anguish that shakes the loins as in labour; the hithpalpel of the verb is the same pattern.

senses.definition: Shaking anguish, filling the loins like the pangs of a woman giving birth.

evidence.note: “My loins are filled with חַלְחָלָה; pangs have seized me like the pangs of a woman giving birth.”
The heart melts, the knees knock together, and חַלְחָלָה is in all loins.
חַלְחָלָה in Cush when the slain fall in Egypt.

words.summary: The round dance of women with timbrels and song, at victories and feasts; once of the calf.

senses.definition: Dancing in a company, with timbrels and singing, in celebration.

evidence.note: All the women went out after Miriam with timbrels וּבִמְחֹלֹת.
The women came out singing וְהַמְּחֹלוֹת to meet Saul, with timbrels.
Jephthah’s daughter came out with timbrels and dances.
“Did they not sing of him בַמְּחֹלוֹת: Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?”
Moses saw the calf וּמְחֹלֹת and broke the tablets.
כִּמְחֹלַת הַמַּחֲנָיִם, like the dance of two camps.

evidence.locator: מְחוֹלָה → χορός ×5 (lemma count), e.g. Exo.15.20 וּבִמְחֹלֹת → χορῶν

evidence.note: The elder son heard music and χορῶν at the lost son’s return.

words.summary: Dancing as the sign of joy, the opposite of mourning, and as praise of Yahweh.

senses.definition: Dancing for joy and in praise, set against mourning.

evidence.note: “You have turned my mourning into מָחוֹל for me; you loosed my sackcloth and girded me with gladness.”
“The joy of our heart has ceased; our מְחֹלֵנוּ is turned to mourning.”
The virgin will rejoice בְּמָחוֹל; “I will turn their mourning into joy.”
“Again you will go forth בִּמְחוֹל of those who make merry.”
“Let them praise his name בְמָחוֹל.”

evidence.locator: מָחוֹל → χορός ×3 (lemma count): Psa.30.12, Psa.149.3, Psa.150.4

opposites.note: “Mourning”, which dancing replaces or into which it is turned.

words.summary: Sand, by the sea, in the measure of what cannot be counted or weighed, and as the bound Yahweh set the sea. It is filed with the root, but its tie to the root’s senses is not yet understood; Jewish Aramaic חָלָא and the Peshitta’s חָלָא are the same word, and no cognate yet shows which older sound stands behind its ח.

senses.definition: The sand of the seashore: a hiding place, a bound for the sea, a weight, and above all a picture of number beyond counting.

evidence.note: “I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens and כַּחוֹל on the shore of the sea.”
“As the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted for multitude.”
“I placed חוֹל as the bound of the sea, a perpetual decree it cannot pass.”
Moses hid the Egyptian בַּחוֹל.
A stone is heavy and sand weighty, but a fool’s vexation is heavier.
Judah and Israel were many כַּחוֹל by the sea, eating, drinking and rejoicing.
Breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore.
“Though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of it will return.” Quoted Rom 9:27.
The seed of David and the Levites multiplied as the sand of the sea.
God’s thoughts, “more than the sand”.
“I shall multiply days כַּחוֹל.”
Isa 10:22 quoted: ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης.
Gen 22:17 recalled: from one man, as good as dead, as the innumerable sand by the seashore.

evidence.locator: חוֹל → ἄμμος ×18 (lemma count); Gen.22.17 כַחוֹל → ὡς τὴν ἄμμον; Isa.10.22, Hos.2.1 → ἄμμος

evidence.note: Gog and Magog, whose number is as the sand of the sea.
The foolish man built his house on the ἄμμον.

parallels.note: “The stars of the heavens”, beside it as the measure of Abraham’s seed.

phrases.gloss: as the sand on the seashore (for multitude)

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܚܝܠܐ (ḥaylā), for δύναμις: God’s power, the power of the spirit, mighty works, strength; and in the plural, armies.

senses.definition: God’s power, given by his spirit, at work in Christ, the gospel and the believers.

evidence.note: “Holy spirit will come, and ܚܝܠܐ of the Most High will overshadow you,” the two lines saying one thing.
“You will receive ܚܝܠܐ when the holy spirit has come upon you.”
“Until you are clothed with ܚܝܠܐ from on high.”
God anointed Jesus with holy spirit and ܚܝܠܐ.
Jesus returned in the ܚܝܠܐ of the spirit to Galilee.
The gospel is the ܚܝܠܐ of God for salvation.
Christ the ܚܝܠܐ of God and the wisdom of God.
“You err, knowing neither the scriptures nor the ܚܝܠܐ of God.”
The Son of man sitting at the right hand of ܚܝܠܐ.
“My ܚܝܠܐ is made perfect in weakness.”

senses.definition: In the plural, works of power: miracles.

evidence.note: The cities in which most of his mighty works were done, which did not repent.
He did not do many mighty works there, because of their unbelief.

senses.definition: In the plural, armed forces: the king’s armies, the armies around Jerusalem, the armies of heaven following the Word of God.

evidence.note: “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies (ܚܝܠܘܬܐ), know that its desolation has come near.”
The king sent his armies and destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
The armies in heaven followed him on white horses.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s verb from ܚܝܠܐ: in the pael to strengthen (ἐνδυναμόω), in the ethpaal to be strengthened, grow strong.

senses.definition: To give strength to someone.

evidence.note: “I am able for all things in Christ who strengthens me.”
“The Lord stood by me and strengthened me.”
An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.

senses.definition: To grow strong, in body, spirit or faith.

evidence.note: The child grew and was strengthened in spirit.
Abraham did not doubt the promise but was strengthened in faith.
“Be strong in the Lord and in the might of his strength.”
Out of weakness were made strong.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܚܝܠܬܢܐ (ḥayltānā), formed from ܚܝܠܐ, for ἰσχυρός.

senses.definition: Strong: of the one coming after John, of God, of an angel, and of the weak made strong.

evidence.note: “One stronger than I comes after me.”
“He who is mighty has done great things for me.”
“Strong is the Lord God who judges her.”
God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
“When I am weak, then I am strong.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܚܠܐ (ḥālā), for ἄμμος, the same word as Hebrew חוֹל; it stands in the New Testament’s quotations of the promise of seed as the sand.

senses.definition: Sand of the seashore: an unstable foundation, and the measure of number.

evidence.note: Isa 10:22: “Though the number of the sons of Israel be as ܚܠܐ of the sea, a remnant will be saved.”
As the ܚܠܐ by the seashore, which cannot be numbered.
The foolish man built his house on ܚܠܐ.

cognates.note: Lane gives حَوْلٌ “strength, power, might, or force; syn. قُوَّةٌ … in the soul and the body and the acquisitions”, as in the saying “there is no strength nor power but by God”, and حَيْلٌ as its dialectal variant with the same meaning and the same saying. This answers to חַיִל as strength (Zec 4:6) and, “in the acquisitions”, to strength gained as wealth (Deu 8:17–18). Arabic ḥ (ح), not ḫ (خ), stands behind ח.

evidence.locator: p. 675, حَوْلٌ (n9582), sense A2
p. 688, حَيْلٌ (n9784), sense b2

cognates.note: In the same Arabic root, حَوْلَ is “around”, حَوْلُ شَىْءٍ the parts round about a thing, and حَوْلٌ also “a year”, named from the revolving of the sun; the verb حَالَ is to change, turn. If it belongs here it gives the circling of the dance and the whirling storm (Jdg 21:21; Jer 23:19), and the rampart that goes round a city (2Sa 20:15). Recorded as possible: Lane draws no link between these and Hebrew, and nothing yet shows whether dance and whirl go with ḥ “strength” or ḫ “labour”.

evidence.locator: p. 675, حَوْلٌ (n9582), senses A1 and A3

cognates.note: The Akkadian verb for a woman’s labour, with ḫayyaltu “woman in labour”: the sense of חוּל “writhe, be in labour” (Isa 26:17; 66:7). Akkadian keeps ḫ and loses ḥ, so the ḫ shows the older sound behind this ח. Oracc writes ḫ as h.

cognates.note: Fisher lists Ugaritic ḫl “go into labor” under *ḫyl, set beside Hebrew חיל “have labor pains, writhe”. Ugaritic keeps ḫ apart from ḥ, so it agrees with Akkadian on ḫ for the sense of labour.

cognates.note: Found only in Neo-Assyrian and later texts, the period when Aramaic words entered Assyrian; it appears to be the Aramaic חֵילָא “army” borrowed, with Akkadian ḫ for foreign ḥ. It shows the army sense was current in the empires that besieged Israel and Judah, but, as a loan, it shows nothing of the older sound.

Num 1:3; plural חֵילַיָּא, חֵילְוָתָא), with a pael חַיֵּיל “strengthen” (Targ. Job 4:4): the same range as Hebrew חַיִל, and the Peshitta’s ܚܝܠܐ. Aramaic ח does not show whether ḥ or ḫ stands behind it.

doctrine.statement: Zerubbabel is told that the house will be finished “not by חַיִל, and not by כֹּחַ, but by my spirit, says Yahweh of hosts” (Zec 4:6): Yahweh’s spirit stands where human strength would stand, as the means by which he works. Gabriel tells Mary, “Holy spirit will come upon you, and power (ܚܝܠܐ, δύναμις) of the Most High will overshadow you” (Luk 1:35), two lines saying one thing. Jesus tells the disciples to wait until they are clothed with power from on high (Luk 24:49), which he names as the holy spirit coming upon them (Act 1:8); Peter says God anointed Jesus “with holy spirit and power” (Act 10:38), and Jesus returned to Galilee “in the power of the spirit” (Luk 4:14). From the verses: the spirit is God’s own power, by which he does what no man’s strength can do.

Israel was warned not to say, “My power and the might of my hand made me this חַיִל”, for “it is he who gives you power to make חַיִל” (Deu 8:17–18). Hannah sings that the bows of the mighty are broken and the stumbling are girded with חַיִל (1Sa 2:4); David says it is God who girds him with חַיִל (Psa 18:33, 40), and Habakkuk, with the fig tree failing, “Yahweh the Lord is my חַיִל” (Hab 3:17–19). A king is not saved by a great חַיִל, nor a horse’s great חַיִל a deliverance (Psa 33:16–17); those who trust in their חַיִל cannot redeem a brother (Psa 49:7–8), and if חַיִל increases the heart is not to be set on it (Psa 62:11). The Lord tells Paul, “My power (ܚܝܠܐ) is made perfect in weakness,” and Paul answers, “When I am weak, then I am strong (ܚܝܠܬܢܐ)” (2Co 12:9–10). From the verses: strength, worth and wealth are God’s gift, and are trusted in only to a man’s loss; the strength that counts is the one God gives to the weak.

Israel confesses, “We were pregnant, we writhed (חַלְנוּ), we gave birth as it were to wind; we have not wrought deliverance in the earth,” and Yahweh answers, “Your dead will live … the earth will cast out the dead” (Isa 26:17–19). Zion brings forth before she writhes, a nation born at once, and Yahweh asks, “Shall I bring to the birth and not cause to bring forth?” (Isa 66:7–9). The barren one “who did not writhe” has more children than the married (Isa 54:1), and Paul quotes this of the Jerusalem above, mother of us all, whose children are, like Isaac, children of promise (Gal 4:26–28). From the verses: the children Zion bears are not the fruit of her own labour but of God’s promise and power, and they come to life by resurrection.

Yahweh swore to Abraham to multiply his seed as the stars of heaven and as the חוֹל on the seashore, and that his seed would possess the gate of his enemies (Gen 22:16–17; 32:13). In Solomon’s day Judah and Israel were many as the sand by the sea (1Ki 4:20), yet Isaiah says, “Though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of it will return” (Isa 10:22), which Paul quotes to show that not all who are of Israel are Israel, but the children of the promise are counted as the seed (Rom 9:6–8, 27). Hebrews counts the sand as already born from one man as good as dead, through faith (Heb 11:11–12), and Jeremiah ties the same measure to the seed of David (Jer 33:22). From the verses: the promise of a seed beyond counting stands, and it is fulfilled in those who are of the faith of Abraham, a remnant out of the natural multitude.

Isaiah sees the חֵיל of the nations come to Zion, its gates open day and night so that men may bring it in (Isa 60:5, 11), and Israel, called priests of Yahweh, eating the חֵיל of the nations (Isa 61:6). Zechariah, after Yahweh’s feet stand on the Mount of Olives and he is king over all the earth, sees the חֵיל of all the nations round about gathered (Zec 14:4, 9, 14); Micah sees daughter Zion devote their חַיִל to the Lord of the whole earth (Mic 4:13). John sees the nations walk in the light of the holy city, the kings of the earth bring their glory into it, and its gates never shut (Rev 21:24–26). From the verses: the kingdom is set up on the earth with Jerusalem at its centre, and the wealth of the nations is brought to it.

Ezekiel prophesies to the slain, and breath comes into them: “they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great חַיִל” (Ezk 37:9–10). Yahweh explains that the bones are the whole house of Israel, who say their hope is lost, and promises, “I will open your graves and bring you up out of your graves, my people, and bring you into the land of Israel … and I will put my spirit in you, and you shall live” (Ezk 37:11–14). From the verses: Israel’s restoration to the land is set forth as a raising from the dead into a living army, and it is Yahweh’s spirit that gives the life.

Nebuchadnezzar and all his חַיִל fought against Jerusalem and its cities, besieged it, and broke it down (Jer 34:1, 7; 39:1; 52:4, 14). Jesus told his disciples, “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies (ܚܝܠܘܬܐ), then know that its desolation has come near … for these are days of vengeance, that all things written may be fulfilled” (Luk 21:20–22), and so it was when Rome’s armies besieged it in AD 70. Ezekiel sees Gog come from the far north in the latter years with a great company, a חַיִל רָב, against the land brought back from the sword, and Yahweh himself judges him there (Ezk 38:8, 15–16, 22). After the thousand years Gog and Magog, as many as the חוֹל of the sea, surround the camp of the saints and the beloved city, and fire from heaven devours them (Rev 20:7–9). From the verses: the army gathered about Jerusalem is a pattern that recurs — Babylon, Rome, Gog at Christ’s coming, and the last uprising — and each time Yahweh brings it to judgment.

In Proverbs 8 the one who speaks is wisdom, who cries at the gates (Pro 8:1–3) and says, “I, wisdom, dwell with prudence” (8:12). She says Yahweh possessed her at the beginning of his way, and that before the depths and the hills she was brought forth, חוֹלָלְתִּי (8:22–25), the verb Moses uses of God bringing forth the earth (Psa 90:2). Eliphaz mocks Job with the same words: “Were you brought forth before the hills? … Do you limit wisdom to yourself?” (Job 15:7–8). Paul says Christ Jesus “was made to us wisdom from God” (1Co 1:30) and calls him God’s power and God’s wisdom (1Co 1:24). From the verses: what was brought forth before the hills is Yahweh’s own wisdom, spoken of as a woman, which he possessed from the beginning; in Christ that wisdom is given to us, but the chapter does not speak of a person existing beside God.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13. The database keys all of BDB’s חוּל and חַיִל words under חול; Biblical Aramaic חַיִל (xh.ah.ad) and the Peshitta’s words are keyed חיל, and the Peshitta’s “sand” חלא. Two older roots in one spelling: ḥ “strength” (Arabic ḥawl, ḥayl) behind חַיִל and the qal “be firm” (Psa 10:5; Job 20:21); ḫ “be in labour” (Akkadian ḫiālu, ḫīlū; Ugaritic ḫl) behind חוּל “writhe, bring forth, tremble”, חִיל, חִילָה, חַלְחָלָה. Not yet placed: whirl and dance (Arabic ḥawl “around” recorded as possible, ḥ), חֵל “rampart”, the sense “wait”, and חוֹל “sand” (Aramaic only, which cannot show ḥ/ḫ). Lead not followed: Ge’ez ḫayl “strength, power” (Anderson–Moser SEM000776 ḫyl “strong”), which would show ḫ against Arabic ḥ for strength; Dillmann and Leslau not checked. Fisher (p. 92) suggests Tigre ḥelā “be strong, overpower” may join the two senses; not followed. Keys: BDB lists the verb’s tokens under both h.bf.aa and h.bg.aa (“be firm”); this entry names h.bf.aa only. חִיל (h.bf.ac) and חִילָה (h.bf.ad) share one token list; h.bf.ac is named on חִיל and חִילָה (Job 6:10) has no key. h.bf.ae (חֵל) is BDB’s list of the construct חֵיל of חַיִל as well as the rampart, so its 63 uses overstate the rampart’s eight or so (2Sa 20:15; 1Ki 21:23; Isa 26:1; Lam 2:8; Nam 3:8; Psa 48:14; 122:7; Oba 1:20 is read as “host”); xh.ah.ad likewise carries Hebrew tokens of the same spelling, and h.bg.ab carries Dan 3:20; 4:11; 4:32; 5:7. Not claimed: h.bf.af חֵילָה (no tokens, cross-reference to חֵל, Psa 48:14), the cross-references h.cd.an, h.cd.ao, h.cg.af, h.ci.ae, h.cp.ag, h.cw.ac, m.bm.ah, m.bn.ak, m.bn.aw. Names: Helon (h.bf.aj) in names/helon.json; places left out: חֵילָם Helam (h.bf.ag, whose key also carries the noun חֵילָם “their wealth”), חֹלוֹן Holon (h.bf.ai), חִילֵן Hilen (h.bf.ah); the Aramaean Hul חוּל (h.bg.ac, Gen 10:23) is a person with no name entry yet. The Psa 10:10 ketiv חֵלְכָּאִים is filed by BDB under חַיִל/חֵל; not entered. Gen 8:10 וַיָּחֶל is entered as piel “wait” but may be יחל. Pro 26:10 is left uncertain. The window חַלּוֹן belongs to another root.
